title: Constant ordinary tensor quotient as the uniformizer-action sheaf cokernel
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with lifted valuation ring $A$ and prescribed lifted uniformizer $p$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $W$ be any scheme and $C_W$ the constant ring sheaf $A_W$. For every $C_W$-module sheaf $N$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and $n\in\mathbf N$, there is an endomorphism $\mu:N\to N$ acting on each section by the constant $p^{n+1}$ and an isomorphism $c:\operatorname{coker}(\mu)\cong (N\otimes_{C_W}(A/(p^{n+1}))_W)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-sp-constant-reduction-models]. The target retains its $C_W$-module structure. The equality $\operatorname{coker}.\pi(\mu)c=\eta_{N,n}$ holds for the published ordinary quotient augmentation $\eta_{N,n}:x\mapsto1\otimes x$. This is a sheaf cokernel, with no assertion of sectionwise surjectivity.

source.place: First paragraph and Comparison with the Stacks Project; ordinary quotient refinement of steps 2, 4 and 6 of lem-sfb-integral-augmented-quotient-towers.

proof.text: The chosen lifted valuation ring A and uniformizer p give the constant quotient coefficient sheaf A/(p^(n+1)). The recorded coefficient comparison identifies its projection with OrderedExchange.quotient. Constant sheafification preserves cokernels, so the regular constant coefficient quotient has this actual projection.

proof.text: For an arbitrary constant-coefficient module sheaf N, multiplication by the constant p^(n+1) is an endomorphism mu. Form its sheaf cokernel. Define a balanced local pairing q(a) tensor x to the class of a*x. Two lifts differ locally by a p^(n+1) multiple and hence give the same class. Sheafification glues these local pairings.

proof.text: The reverse map sends the class of x to 1 tensor x. It kills p^(n+1)*x since that scalar vanishes in the quotient. The two composites fix the local quotient classes and pure tensors; sheafification therefore gives inverse sheaf-module maps. The tensor-side inverse is the actual ordinary augmentation by its section formula.

lean.statement:
theorem constantQuotientCokernel
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (W : Scheme.{u})
    (N : reductionModules W (exchangeConstantRing W (PbcIntegralRing l E))) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ μ : End N,
      (∀ (Z : W.ProEtᵒᵖ) (x : N.val.obj Z),
        μ.val.app Z x =
          @SMul.smul ((exchangeConstantRing W (PbcIntegralRing l E)).obj.obj Z)
            (N.val.obj Z) inferInstance
            ((toSheafify (ProEt.topology W)
              ((Functor.const W.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj (CommRingCat.of (PbcIntegralRing l E)))).app Z
                ((pbcUniformizer l E) ^ (n + 1))) x) ∧
      ∃ c : cokernel μ ≅ ((OrderedExchange.reductionModule (pbcIntegralDatum l E) W).obj
          N).obj (op n),
        cokernel.π μ ≫ c.hom =
          ((OrderedExchange.ordinaryAugmentation (pbcIntegralDatum l E) W).app N).app
            (op n)
